target_customer: Music fans and artists at launch, later celebrity YouTube channel owners and the advertisers who wanted their audiences
problem: Fans had no single place to keep track of the latest music and videos from their favorite artists, and artists lacked a simple way to release them. After the 2013 relaunch the problem became helping celebrities grow YouTube subscribers.
business_model: Free consumer discovery site at launch; after April 2013 a YouTube multi channel network taking a share of advertising revenue (inferred from the network model, not a stated rate)
product_category: Music discovery, later YouTube multi channel network

founders.name: Bryan Kim
founders.background_notes: YC page lists past Ustream and Hipset, current BackerKit. Education not found.

founders.name: Mazy Kazerooni
founders.background_notes: YC page lists no background. Hypebot coverage names him as co-creator of Tracks.by.

founders.name: Matt Schlicht
founders.background_notes: Not on the YC page; named by Hypebot and TechCrunch coverage as the Tracks.by and Hipset co-founder quoted on the 2013 relaunch.

competitors.traction_then: not stated in the source snippet

technical_complexity.rationale: A web app that aggregated artist links and Facebook likes into a feed was standard web engineering for a two person team in 2012; the later MCN model was an operations and licensing problem, not a technical one.

defensibility.rationale: Music discovery feeds were easy to copy and the artist relationships were not exclusive. The pivot to a YouTube network rested on signed celebrity channels, which had no structural lock in.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent copied or bought it in the sources found. The 2013 pivot moved it into the crowded YouTube multi channel network space; no later outcome is documented.

market_need_then: Fans were consuming music through Facebook likes and YouTube, and artists wanted ways to reach them; Hypebot and TechCrunch covered the discovery category heavily in 2012. No spend or demand figures were found.

branding.domain_note: Operated by TracksBy; the YC listing website is tracksby.com, which returned HTTP 503 when fetched. Domain purchase history not found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Co-founder Matt Schlicht told Hypebot the network would not push Hipset branding and would focus on the artists.

rebrands.why: Team moved from discovery to a YouTube network for celebrities; name kept

branding.community_and_virality: TechCrunch and Hypebot covered the launch and the 2013 relaunch with artists such as Daughtry and Soulja Boy; a Hypebot piece covered a Facebook likes feature in 2012. No merch or fan community found.

brand_strength.rationale: Some trade press and celebrity signings, but the name resembled other hip prefixed startups and the founders said they would downplay the brand in favor of artists.

pivots.to: YouTube network for celebrity channels (Hipset Network, Hipset Boost tool)
pivots.why: Discovery site did not break out; relaunch signed artists to grow YouTube subscribers (TechCrunch and Hypebot coverage)

outcome_analysis: Hipset launched in summer 2012 as a music discovery site by the Tracks.by team and had raised seed money from angels by then. By April 2013 it had morphed into a YouTube network for celebrity channels, a crowded category. CB Insights lists it as dead and YC marks it inactive, but no shutdown announcement or stated cause is public, so the failure factors are inferred from the pivot and the category rather than a company statement.
notes: Company site tracksby.com returned 503, so it was not confirmed live. The cause of failure is not public. The $1M April 2013 seed and the $1.61M total over four rounds rest on CB Insights alone, so about $0.61M across earlier rounds is a gap I could not source. Audrey Capital (Matt Mullenweg) lists Hipset in its 2012 portfolio and marks it defunct. A search snippet attributed Menlo Ventures and Alexis Ohanian as investors but I found no source that confirms it, so they are not recorded. Matt Schlicht was added as co-founder from press coverage, not from the YC page.
